Verify and report formatting + lint findings (the CI gate, no writes), or with `--fix` apply every safe fix — whitespace, style, analyzer, and lint (CST) — in one pass. Bare `dotnet-fast <path>` runs the report.

lint's ported-analyzer rules (`SA*`/`RCS*`/`S*`/`MA*`/`AV*`/`GU*`/`PH*`/ `VSTHRD*`/xUnit*/NUnit* — StyleCop/Roslynator/Sonar/Meziantou/CSharpGuidelines/ etc. reimplementations) are a bundled SUPERSET, always on by default regardless of which analyzer packages the project actually references — they are NOT restricted to what a real `dotnet build`/`dotnet format` would surface for that project, and can therefore report rule IDs `dotnet format` never would. Built-in families (`CA*`/`IDE*`/`SYSLIB*`) and the native `DFxxxx` catalog always mirror `dotnet format`. Pass `--only-active-analyzers` to restrict the ported rules to packages the project actually references (a stricter parity check, not the default).

Usage: dotnet-fast lint [OPTIONS] [TARGET]

Arguments:
  [TARGET]
          Project, solution, or folder to format. Defaults to the current directory

Options:
  -?, --help
          Show help and usage information
          
          [alias: -h]

      --fix
          Apply every safe fix — whitespace, style, analyzer, and lint (CST) — in one pass, instead of only reporting. Without `--fix`, `lint` verifies and reports, writing nothing and exiting non-zero on any finding (the gate)

      --check
          Verify only (the default): make no changes and exit non-zero on any finding. Accepted as an explicit, self-documenting form of bare `lint`; cannot be combined with `--fix`

      --version
          Show version information

      --fix-safe-only
          Like `--fix`, but apply only Safe-tier CST (`lint`) autofixes — the redundancy/style cleanups — and hold back behavior-preserving (performance) and suggestion (correctness/concurrency/maintainability) rewrites for review. Whitespace/style/analyzer formatting still applies. `--list-rules`/`--explain` show each rule's tier

      --affected
         
[truncated]

Determine projects affected by a set of Git changes

Usage: dotnet-fast affected [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  generate  Generate affected project output files. This is also the default when no command is supplied
  describe  Print changed and affected projects without writing output files
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -?, --help
          Show help and usage information
          
          [alias: -h]

      --ignore-changed <PATH>...
          Ignore changes to these paths when deciding what is affected (issue #234). Repeatable; each value is a repo-relative path or a glob (`NuGet.Config`, `config/*.json`, `**/*.md`).
          
          For CI harnesses that must REWRITE a tracked file before the tool runs — swapping in an agent-specific `NuGet.Config`, for example. `affected` compares the working tree, so such a rewrite is a genuine change and fans out exactly as a real edit to that file would; a shared feed config reaches every project. This drops those paths from the changed set.
          
          NOTE: the global `--exclude` does NOT do this — it filters the resulting project set, not the changed files.
          
          Every ignored file is reported on stderr: silently discarding a change is how a build under-builds and ships something untested, so it is never quiet.

  -p, --repository-path <PATH>
          Path to the Git repository root. Defaults to the current repository

      --version
          Show version information

      --solution-path <PATH>
          Solution file used to limit project discovery

      --from <REV>
          Branch or commit to compare against --to, or against the working tree when --to is omitted

      --to <REV>
          Branch or commit to compare against --from

      --merge-base
          Compare from the merge base of --from and --to instead of directly from --from

      --ci
          Detect the comparison range from the CI environment (GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines, GitLab CI, or Jenkins): pull-re

Use `--write` to append it to `<target>/.editorconfig`. Addresses the opt-out firehose: a fresh `lint` surfaces real defects instead of tens of thousands of style warnings. Pass `--guardrails` for a different profile: every AI-guardrail rule (`DF9001`-`DF9008`) enabled at the published code-health budget numbers, so adopting that family is one command instead of six rules and five thresholds set by hand

Usage: dotnet-fast editorconfig recommend [OPTIONS] [TARGET]

Arguments:
  [TARGET]
          Directory whose `.editorconfig` to append to with `--write`. Defaults to the current directory

Options:
  -?, --help
          Show help and usage information
          
          [alias: -h]

      --write
          Append the profile to `<target>/.editorconfig` instead of printing it

      --guardrails
          Emit the AI-guardrail adoption profile (`DF9001`-`DF9008` at the published code-health budget numbers) instead of the ported-analyzer profile

      --version
          Show version information

Global options:
      --project <PROJECT>
          Limit a solution run to specific project paths or project names

      --include <PATH>...
          Relative file or folder paths to include

      --exclude <PATH>...
          Relative file or folder paths to exclude

      --include-generated
          Include generated source files

      --no-restore
          Accepted for dotnet format CLI compatibility. Restore is never performed

      --report <REPORT_DIR>
          Directory to receive a JSON report

      --verify-no-changes
          Verify that no formatting changes would be performed

      --diff
          Preview the would-be rewrite as a unified diff (git-apply-able) without writing any file. Shows whitespace, style, and `lint --fix` (CST) edits in one patch. Exits non-zero when any file would change

Options:
  -?, --help
          Show help and usage information
          
          [alias: -h]

      --scope <BRANCH>
          Branch/scope whose history to read. Defaults to the current git branch (or `DOTNET_FAST_TIMINGS_SCOPE`), matching the recording side

      --env <ENV>
          Read the `ci` or `local` timings partition (#194) instead of auto-detecting from the invoking shell. Lets a local shell read data a CI run recorded, e.g. `--env ci` to see what your Azure Pipelines/GitHub Actions run found without re-running it
          
          [possible values: ci, local]

      --version
          Show version information

      --top <N>
          Show only the top N slowest entries (0 = all). Default 20
          
          [default: 20]

      --baseline-scope <BRANCH>
          Compare `--scope` against this baseline scope and report the regression diff (slower/faster/new/missing) instead of the hotspots list. Typically the default branch, e.g. `--baseline-scope main`

      --threshold <PCT>
          Regression-diff threshold: only report units whose time moved by more than this percent (ignored without `--baseline-scope`). Default 10
          
          [default: 10]

      --json
          Emit a machine-readable JSON document instead of the text table

      --html <FILE>
          Write a self-contained HTML report to this file (inline CSS, no external requests — opens straight from a CI artifact). Text still prints to stdout unless `--json` is also given
